overall_why: B over A: B is the most finished and consistent piece of design, and it carries the two feelings that decide whether an ADHD student starts at all. The rest surface is three lines and a caret in one 66-character Charter column (concept-b/shots/s1-cold-light, s5-week-dark), and Return started the lesson at once in my real-window turn. Every secondary place is the same 620 px layer with a line to type in, a list and a key row: setup, courses, plan, material, settings and help (concept-b/shots/setup-signed-out-dark, courses-light, plan-dark, settings-light, help-light). Every grey I sampled passes AA in both schemes. A is the stronger workspace: its split-pane plan with change bars and struck old dates is the best single answer to scenario 3 (concept-a/shots/s3-after-light, concept-a/view/live/s3-after-light). But A carries the most chrome of the three (tab row, status line, bold 26 px H1, filled blue button: concept-a/shots/s1-cold-light). It keeps the 'Your answer' label the brief asked to remove (concept-a/shots/s2-answer-light). Its pinned task strip collides with the scrolled task underneath (concept-a/shots/s4-offplan-light). In the real window, Return on its cold 'New lesson' page did nothing, and my next keystrokes became the lesson's title. What tipped it to B: B's faults are polish (a top fade and a repeated foot line), while A's are in the first keystroke and the main lesson view. A over C: C has the nicest single idea, the record's marks set as marginalia beside the answer (concept-c/shots/s2-answer-light), and its plan agenda updates in place. But it has the most rendering and layout faults: raw '$V_{max}$' (concept-c/shots/course-light), 'K m' (concept-c/shots/stop-dark), a column off-centre on the cold page (concept-c/shots/s1-cold-light), two sheet widths with no scrim, and a 'back to the task' that returns to an already-answered task (concept-c/shots/s4-return-light). In the real window its ⌘K sheet did not focus its search field.

by_measure_why.mine: A is literally the client's reference tools. Your files open in tabs and in a sidebar (concept-a/shots/sidebar-dark), your own Markdown is rendered beside the lesson (concept-a/shots/material-light), settings are a plain text file (concept-a/shots/settings-light), and the cold open shows your half-written answer still under the question (concept-a/shots/s1-cold-light). In my turn, ⌘K 'light' switched the scheme instantly. B is a close second and recedes further. Its settings layer previews each face in itself and has 'Edit as text…' for any font, colour or key (concept-b/shots/settings-light). Arrow keys changed the scheme live in my turn, and the app's own voice is a 12.5–13 px SF line. A edges it because B's first-run and rest screens still speak in the app's sentences, while A shows the learner's own documents. C offers only face, size, scheme and line length (concept-c/shots/settings-light). Its sheets put focus on 'Close' rather than on a field, and the date heading on every page is the app's voice, not the learner's material.
by_measure_why.calm: B's cold surface is a course label, one title, one 'where you stopped' line and a caret: no chrome at all (concept-b/shots/s1-cold-dark). Its lessons are one column with no sidebar or bars (concept-b/shots/s4-offplan-light). C's cold page is calm too: a date, one line and a field (concept-c/shots/s1-cold-light). In a lesson, though, it adds a time gutter, a right-hand agenda, a five-item action row under every task and a second writing line (concept-c/shots/s2-start-light). A always shows a tab row and a status line. Its cold screen has a bold 26 px H1, a 'The lesson so far' label, the task, a faded draft and a filled blue button (concept-a/shots/s1-cold-light), and scenario 3 splits the window in two (concept-a/shots/s3-after-light).
by_measure_why.easy_to_start: B: one Return, with the caret already in the line and '↩ carry on' at its end (concept-b/shots/s1-cold-light). After a week it names the first thing by skill and date, never by count (concept-b/shots/s5-week-light). In my turn, Return started the lesson at once. C: 'Pick up where you stopped on Tuesday' with a Return keycap (concept-c/shots/s1-cold-light), which also started at once in my turn. It ranks second because it gives you two lines to choose between (the suggestion and 'Or write your own first line'), and after a week it names the gap date in full (concept-c/shots/s5-week-light). A's evidence is strong: a 'Continue Return' button with your draft above it (concept-a/shots/s5-week-light). But in the real window, Return on the cold 'New lesson' page did nothing because focus was on the page body. The next thing I typed became the lesson's title ('b = 5'), the worst possible failure for someone for whom starting is the hard part.
by_measure_why.flexible: A changes the plan where you can see it. The plan document opens in a second pane with ochre change bars, 'moved up' and 'moved down', and the old dates struck through. It did this in the demo, the live lesson and my turn (concept-a/shots/s3-after-light, concept-a/view/live/s3-after-light). The open task pins to the top, and Tab takes you back. After a reply with no task, the caret moved to talk by itself. C's right-margin agenda changes in place ('Moved from Sun 22 Nov', 'moved up', 'moved down': concept-c/view/window/s3-after-light), and its talk line is always visible under the task, so you can see where talk goes. B shows a good inline 'The plan changed' card (concept-b/shots/s3-after-light), but it collapses into a grey line one turn later (s4-offplan-light). Talk needs Esc first. In all three windows, a plan change typed straight in while a task was open was filed as an answer and showed 'no mark'. B's 'no mark' sat right under my plan request, which reads worst; C's visible talk line at least shows the alternative.
by_measure_why.craft: B: one ink (#2F3F86 / #9AA9EE) and four neutrals, Charter for the material and tutor, SF for you and the app. It has a clear 12.5/14/17/21/27 scale, one layer component everywhere, and every sampled grey is ≥4.3:1 even after anti-aliasing (the 'esc talk instead' hint is 4.3–4.9:1). Its faults: the top fade leaves the course eyebrow as half-clipped ghost glyphs at y≈65 on every lesson screen (concept-b/shots/s2-start-light, s5-week-next-light). The pinned open task cuts running text with a hard edge (concept-b/view/live/s3-before-light, shots/narrow-lesson-dark). The task rule and answer-line rule are two bars with an 8 px gap. In the plan layer, the changed-row tint is almost the same as the selection (plan-dark). A: a strong hierarchy (bold serif titles, blue 'your ink' for the learner's words, ticks and crosses in the gutter, ochre for change) and good narrow behaviour (narrow-lesson-light). But the pinned strip overlaps the scrolled task, leaving 'Your answer' glyphs and two left rules at x=197 and x=214, with its text at about 2.3:1 (s4-offplan-light/dark). The tab sits 12 px from the traffic lights in split view (concept-a/view/window/s3-after-light). 'Vmax' is plain in the sidebar, palette and new-lesson field but typeset in the tabs, the cold draft is 3.6:1 in light, and the settings tab went stale after ⌘K changed the scheme. C: the gutter marginalia are lovely and its tokens are documented (margin grey 4.7:1). But it shows raw LaTeX (course-light), 'K m' (stop-dark), 's/ μM' split over a line break (s5-week-next-light), an off-centre cold column, two sheet widths with no scrim cutting the page mid-word (plan-light, courses-dark), a PDF page flush to the sheet edge (source-dark), and a placeholder at 2.7:1.
by_measure_why.clarity: A tells you the most, and in the right place. 'Stopped on Tue 10 Nov at 16:40. Continue Return' on the cold screen (s1-cold-light). 'The tutor is writing', 'Plan changed at 18:15' and 'Tab: back to the task' in the status line (s3-before-light, s3-after-light). In my turn it even explained a missing mark: 'No mark, not taken as the answer' and '× Not right yet, with a hint'. B is honest and clear but terse. The foot band repeats the last fact under the next question, so 'Marked right, on your own.' sits under a new, unanswered task (concept-b/shots/s2-answer-light, concept-b/view/live/c3-answer-1-light). '⌘K start without them' refers to a 'them' never shown (s5-week-light). And in the live run the plan change showed only as the foot line, before the tutor's reply appeared (concept-b/view/live/s3-after-dark). C makes you choose between two writing lines at every task. Its demo 'back to the task' re-posed the already-answered Vmax question (s4-return-light). In the live run the talk line had scrolled off-screen after the plan change (concept-c/view/live/s3-after-light).
by_measure_why.performance: Input latency is identical in window/perf.json: median 17 ms, p95 19, max 20 for all three. On startup (first/main/week), A is 809/628/575 ms (mean 671), B 850/620/567 (mean 679) and C 805/615/644 (mean 688). In my own turns, the perf op measured A's startup at 623 ms, B's at 837 and C's at 835, with input median 17 for all three. A is first on both. B edges C on the evidence mean, mainly because C's week reopen (644 ms) is the slowest return of the three. All the differences are small, and B and C are within noise of each other.

concept-a: The pinned open-task strip is drawn on top of the scrolled task. 'Your answer' glyphs show through under it, two left rules sit at different x (197 and 214), and its text is about 2.3:1, below AA (concept-a/shots/s4-offplan-light, s4-offplan-dark).

The answer field still says 'Your answer', the label the brief asked to replace. In the real window, Return on the cold 'New lesson' page did nothing (focus was on the page body), so my next keystrokes became the lesson's title 'b = 5'.

It is too heavy and inconsistent for 'calm': a tab row, a status line, a bold 26 px H1 and a filled button on the cold screen (s1-cold-light). Tabs crowd the traffic lights in split view (view/window/s3-after-light). 'Vmax' is plain text in the sidebar and palette but typeset in the tabs (sidebar-dark, open-light). The settings file still read 'scheme = dark' after ⌘K had switched to light.
concept-b: The top fade leaves the course eyebrow as half-clipped ghost text on every lesson screen (concept-b/shots/s2-start-light, s5-week-next-light, reopen-dark). The pinned foot band cuts running paragraphs with a hard edge instead of fading them (concept-b/view/live/s3-before-light, shots/narrow-lesson-dark).

The foot band repeats what is already on screen: 'Marked right, on your own.' twice (s2-answer-light), and the plan change as both a card and a blue line (s3-after-light). Under a fresh question it reads as if that question had been marked.

Answering is the default place. A plan change typed straight in was filed as an answer with 'no mark' under it (my turn). The task and the answer line have two separate rules with an 8 px gap. In the plan layer, changed rows are tinted almost like the selected row (plan-dark), and 'Your work' truncates the skill name to make room for metadata (work-light).
concept-c: Rendering faults: raw '$V_{max}$' in the course sheet (concept-c/shots/course-light), 'K m' in the stop line (stop-dark), the unit 's/ μM' split across a line (s5-week-next-light), and a PDF page flush against the sheet's right edge (source-dark).

Layout drifts between states. The column is off-centre whenever the agenda is absent (135 px left, 294 px right: s1-cold-light). Sheets come in two widths with no scrim, so they cut the page mid-word (plan-light vs courses-dark). The task appears with and without a 'Task' label (s4-return-light vs s2-start-light), and the same moment is stamped 18:05 in one scheme and 18:06 in the other (s4-offplan).

Too much at each task: two writing lines plus a five-item action row, with the talk placeholder at 2.7:1 (s2-start-light). Its ⌘K and ⌘P sheets put focus on 'Close' instead of a field, so in my turn I could not type into the command list. The demo's 'back to the task' returned to an already-answered question (s4-return-light).

window_turns: I did the same in each window: open cold, press Return, 'b = 5', 'Can I have a hint?', 'b = -5', then the stand-in's own right answer. Then I typed 'I skipped three days and the midterm moved, change the plan' straight into whatever line had the caret, then 'By the way, what is a z-score?' and 'OK, back to the task.', then perf, ⌘P, ⌘, and ⌘K. B: cold showed 'Intro Statistics / Sampling distributions / the standard error of a mean…' with the caret in the line, and Return started the lesson. 'b = 5' showed 'Not right yet.' under the answer and again under the line. The hint went as talk. The later tries showed no mark, which matches the record (it marks only a first try). The plan request went into the answer line and showed 'no mark' under it. Then the tutor's reply came with a 'The plan changed' card (Midterm 2 Sun 22 → Sun 29 Nov) and ⌘P. Off-plan and back went as talk. ⌘P showed the moved rows, ⌘K focused its field, and ⌘, settings were fully arrow-key operable: I switched to Dark live and back to 'Like the Mac'. Perf: startup 837 ms, input median 17 / p95 19. C: cold showed 'Start on Midterm 2' with a Return keycap, and Return started the lesson. 'b = 5' put 'not right' in the margin, the hint was recognised, and the retry got 'no mark' in the margin. The plan request typed in the exercise line was filed inside the task as an answer, but the right-hand agenda updated in place (Sun 29 Nov, 'Moved from Sun 22 Nov', moved up/down) and a timed 'The plan changed' line appeared. Off-plan and back also went as answers because the caret stayed in the exercise. ⌘P and ⌘, opened sheets with focus on 'Close'. ⌘K opened Commands with no field focused, so typing 'dark' failed. Perf: startup 835 ms, input 17 / 20. A: cold showed 'New lesson / What do you want to work on?' with 'Sampling distributions' suggested, but Return did nothing (focus on the body), so 'b = 5' became the lesson title. The tutor then posed the task. The hint showed 'You asked for a hint.', 'b = -5' showed '× Not right yet, with a hint' in the gutter, and the right answer showed '– No mark, not taken as the answer'. The plan request typed in the answer line was filed as an answer (no mark), then the plan opened in a split pane with change bars and struck dates, and the status line read 'Plan changed at 19:00 · Tab: back to the task'. The caret then moved to talk, so off-plan and back went as talk. ⌘, opened settings.conf as a tab, and ⌘K 'light' switched the scheme instantly, but the open file still read 'scheme = dark'. Perf: startup 623 ms, input 17 / 18.
